topic: From Motion to Math: Understanding the Derivative
target_audience: High school students or early university students (Calculus I beginners)

sections.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
sections.content: Introduce the concept of motion. While average speed is easy to calculate (total distance / total time), how do we determine the speed at one exact, 'frozen' moment in time? This introduces the need for the instantaneous rate of change.
sections.example: An animation of a Cheetah chasing a gazelle. A graph of its position f(t) vs. time (t) appears next to it. We see the cheetah accelerating, and a 'speedometer' icon fluctuates wildly.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Slope and Average Rate
sections.content: Review the concept of the 'Secant Line'. To find average speed between two points (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)), we calculate the slope: (f(b) - f(a)) / (b - a). This is the foundation for the derivative.
sections.example: On the Cheetah's position graph, two points A and B are marked. A blue straight line (secant) connects them. The slope formula is shown clearly on screen as 'Rise over Run'.

sections.title: The Concept of 'h': Zooming In
sections.content: Instead of using 'a' and 'b', let's use 'x' and 'x + h', where 'h' is the interval between two points. To find the speed at exactly 'x', we must make the interval 'h' smaller and smaller.
sections.example: An animation shows point B sliding down the curve toward point A. The distance between them, labeled 'h', shrinks from a wide gap to a tiny sliver.

sections.title: The Limit: The Magic of Zero
sections.content: The 'Instantaneous' paradox: if h = 0, we are dividing by zero, which is impossible. We introduce the Limit notation. We don't make h zero; we look at what happens as h 'approaches' zero.
sections.example: The secant line rotates as point B gets closer to A. Just as h nearly vanishes, the line turns from blue (secant) to red (tangent), touching the curve at exactly one point.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formally introduce the derivative formula: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain that this result is a new function that gives the slope (instantaneous rate) at any point x.
sections.example: A 'Function Machine' visual. Input: The position curve f(x) = x². Process: Apply the limit formula. Output: f'(x) = 2x. A table shows that at time t=3, the cheetah's instantaneous speed is 6 m/s.

sections.title: Visual Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap that the derivative is simply the 'slope of the tangent line.' Mention applications beyond motion, such as marginal cost in economics or cooling rates in physics.
sections.example: A split-screen view: Left side shows a car's speedometer (instantaneous speed); right side shows the slope of the tangent line on the car's distance-time graph, moving in perfect synchronization.
